_note: WHETHER A MODEL LOADS IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE MODEL. It is a property of (model x environment), and this file keys it that way because the v3 grid proved the point twice in one night: LLM360/AmberSafe failed and then succeeded on the SAME BOX after two packages were installed, and thirteen checkpoints that load without complaint on this Mac are unloadable on an A100 because of a torch version floor. A registry field like `needs_torch` is a summary of these observations, not a substitute for them -- so the observations live here and the summary is derived.

fields.packages_present: measured -- only those that turned out to MATTER
fields.packages_absent: measured -- absence that CAUSED a failure

fields.fix: declared -- what made it load, where known

_provenance.note: Observations are recorded when seen. Absence of an observation means UNTESTED, never 'works' -- eight of the thirteen torch-floor models were predicted from the weights audit before the run reached them, and are marked predicted rather than observed.

grid_v3_box_initial.note: vast.ai instance 46301965 as provisioned. requirements.txt was never installed on it -- sentencepiece and protobuf are DECLARED in the repo and were simply missing.

grid_v3_box_repaired.note: Same box after installing the two declared packages mid-run. tiktoken was DELIBERATELY NOT installed: transformers was falling back to a TikToken extractor for a SentencePiece file, and installing it would have let the WRONG converter succeed silently. The LOAD FAILED was protective.

local_mps.note: Loads every .bin checkpoint the box refuses, because torch >= 2.6 satisfies check_torch_load_is_safe.

observations.cause: SentencePieceExtractor requires the protobuf library -> falls back to TikToken extractor -> `tiktoken` is required
observations.fix: pip install sentencepiece protobuf. The first error named sentencepiece; after installing it the error CHANGED to name protobuf. Following the message beat guessing.
verified before scoring: vocab 32000, ids IDENTICAL to LLM360/Amber on 4 probes incl. Chinese and a literary prompt

observations.cause: torch.load refusal; safetensors shards PRESENT but model.safetensors.index.json ABSENT, so transformers falls back to the .bin index
observations.fix: scripts/repair_safetensors_index.py rebuilds the index from the shard headers over HTTP range requests. use_safetensors=True does NOT help -- the flag selects a format, it does not synthesise the map.
verified interactively: 1.48B params, no complaint. THIS IS THE OBSERVATION THAT IDENTIFIED THE CAUSE -- RH asked why a model runs on MPS and not on the bigger machine.
32B at fp16 fits an 80GB card at ~93% VRAM (76,113 MiB) and scores at ~1.0 p/s. Purge-before-download held: 247 GB disk free with the model resident.

observations.cause: MY BUG, not the environment: assert_prompt_survives decoded without skip_special_tokens, so the guard failed the prompt against the BOS its own policy had added. Mistral/Llama-family tokenizers only.
observations.fix: skip_special_tokens=True in the guard; all five affected models rescored

predicted_untested.note: From data/weights_audit.csv, not from observation. bin-only checkpoints that the run had not yet reached. Listed so absence of an observation is never read as success.

provisioning_lessons: INSTALL requirements.txt ON THE BOX. sentencepiece and protobuf were declared in the repo and absent from the instance; that alone cost one model and an hour.
PIN torch >= 2.6, or thirteen checkpoints in the 103-model spec are unloadable and the cause reads like a transformers policy.
DO NOT install tiktoken to silence a SentencePiece conversion error. It lets the wrong converter succeed on a SentencePiece file, turning a loud failure into a quiet one.

Library versions are an INSTRUMENT dimension. Local vs box on one shared model: identical surface set, per-word probabilities differing by <=1.5e-3. Small, not zero -- cells now stamp torch_version and transformers_version.
The box ran 5.14.1 while every precondition was established locally on 5.4.0. An encode guarantee established on a different library version than the run uses is not a guarantee.
